You know how this goes.

A client sends an export. Half the dates are text. The same customer is spelled four different ways. Somebody typed N/A into a number column. You open the file, sigh, and clear the afternoon.

  • Hours of find and replace

    The same fixes, again, for every new file that lands in your inbox.

  • Formulas nobody can read

    Last month's cleanup sheet falls apart the moment a column moves.

  • Mistakes found too late

    A duplicate row or a shifted column makes it into the report before anyone notices.

With The God's Tool you upload the file, read the list of problems it found, and approve the fixes. Save those steps once and run them again on next month's file.

What you actually get

Connect it, clean it, set it to repeat. That's most of it.

  • Plain English cleaning

    Type something like "make every date YYYY-MM-DD" or "treat Acme Inc and ACME as one customer". It writes the step and shows you the result before anything changes.

  • A list of what's wrong

    Each column is scanned for blanks, duplicates, odd values and mixed formats. You see the full list first, then decide.

  • Works with what you already use

    CSV files, Google Sheets, MySQL, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, MongoDB, AWS, Databricks, Google Analytics 4 and more.

  • Steps you can reuse

    Save a cleanup once and run it on every new file. Put it on a schedule if you'd rather not think about it.

  • SQL you can see and edit

    Every step has SQL behind it. Copy it, change it, or write your own in the built-in editor.

  • Alerts before reports break

    Get an email when a column changes shape or the numbers start to look off.

  • Private databases, handled

    Reach a database behind a firewall through a secure tunnel. You don't open any ports.

  • Teams and approvals

    Admin, Data Steward, Editor and Viewer roles. Sensitive sources can sit behind an approval step.

  • Private AI mode by default

    Plain English cleaning works from the shape of your data, such as column types and value patterns. By default your rows and cell values stay on our side and are not sent to the AI. An admin can choose to share a few sample rows.

Three steps. That's it.

  1. Add your data

    Upload a CSV, paste a Google Sheet link, or connect a database.

  2. Check what it found

    Every problem is listed by column. Accept the fixes you like and describe the rest in your own words.

  3. Download or repeat

    Grab the clean file, send it to a destination, or save the steps to run again later.

Know when your data changes

Schedule a run and get an email if a column disappears, a type flips or the values drift. You hear about it before your client does.

Questions people ask

What does The God's Tool do?

It cleans messy data. You upload a CSV or connect a Google Sheet or database, it lists the problems it finds, and you approve the fixes or describe your own in plain English. The steps can be saved and run again.

Can I clean a CSV or Google Sheet for free?

Yes. The free plan handles CSV files up to 5 MB and 5,000 rows per run, with up to 3 sources and 1 pipeline. New accounts also get 14 days with every feature included.

Do I need to know SQL or code?

No. You can do all of it by clicking and typing in plain English. If you do know SQL, every step shows the query behind it and you can edit it.

What are credits, and who are they for?

One credit covers one AI action, like asking it to write a cleaning step. They're useful if you only clean data now and then, because there is no monthly fee. They cost about $0.03 each, with a $2 minimum top-up.

Can I use it for client work?

Yes, many freelancers do. The files are processed under your account, so check that your agreement with the client allows sharing their data with a tool like this.

Is my data safe?

Data is encrypted in transit and we don't sell it or share it for marketing. Google sign-in is only used to log you in, and a Google Sheet is read only when you connect it yourself. The AI features run in private mode: they get your instruction, column names and a summary of each column's structure, never your actual rows. Read how it works in plain words, with diagrams, on our blog, or see the privacy policy for the details.

Does the AI see my data?

Not by default. The AI gets your instruction and a description of each column's structure, then writes cleaning steps that we run on our side. Your rows and cell values aren't sent to it. A workspace admin can switch on sharing a few sample rows for better results on value-based fixes, and it stays off until they do. The blog post "How AI cleaning works without ever seeing your data" explains the whole path with diagrams.

Which data sources can I connect?

CSV, Google Sheets, MySQL, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, MongoDB, AWS RDS, S3, DynamoDB and Redshift, Google Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Databricks, REST APIs and Google Analytics 4.

What happens when the trial ends?

Your account moves to the free plan with its limits. Nothing is deleted, and you can upgrade or buy credits whenever you like.

How does a quote work?

Fill in the short form on this page. We read it and reply by email with a price for credits, seats or sources. There's no obligation to buy.
